channel.title: Clinovian Insights
channel.description: Source-bounded clinical denial analysis by Clinovian.

item.title: The Two-Midnight Rule: Why Most Observation Appeals Fail
item.description: CMS’s Two-Midnight Rule is prospective. Most appeals treat it as retrospective. That’s why they lose.

item.title: Six Failure Modes of Clinical Denial Appeals
item.description: Why most medical-necessity appeals fail — and the six patterns behind it. From generic narratives to missed criteria pathways to deadline expiry.

item.title: Post-Acute Denials: What Federal Oversight Data Shows
item.description: Federal data on Medicare Advantage post-acute denial rates and appeal outcomes. What the patterns mean for denial teams.

item.title: Inpatient vs. Observation: Where Level-of-Care Denials Turn
item.description: Why observation-status downgrades are one of the most consistently under-argued denial categories, and what criteria-mapped appeals look like.

item.title: What AI Appeal Tools Get Wrong
item.description: Five patterns of clinical error in AI-generated medical-necessity appeals. Why physician QA matters before submission.

item.title: DRG Downgrades: The Revenue Your Dashboard Doesn't Show
item.description: Paid-but-downgraded DRG claims are invisible in denial dashboards. Why they exist, how to find them, and what clinical-coding crossover reasoning looks like.

item.title: Behavioral Health Denials: Why "Still Symptomatic" Loses
item.description: Behavioral health denials are systematically under-appealed. The clinical argument required differs from med-surg denials — and most appeal teams miss it.

item.title: 2026 Federal IDR Rule: What It Commoditizes — and What It Does Not
item.description: What the 2026 Federal IDR Operations final rule changes and why complex disputes still need physician-authored clinical evidence.
